source.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
source.authors: Ananth Eswar; Pratinav Seth; Utsav Avaiya; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

page_placements.theme: Sparse components carry refusal: neurons, weight rows, attention-head groups, SAE/transcoder features, MoE experts

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that two attribution methods install refusal using largely disjoint neuron-row masks, and interprets this as evidence for a redundant refusal subspace rather than a unique mechanism. This refines the single-direction account, although it does not intervene on a residual-stream direction.
record.gate_note: The study's own behavior-level interventions and mask-overlap results are recorded for V4. It does not apply the original difference-in-means residual-stream direction or test its all-layer ablation/addition. Language-modeling selector-audit results are outside the listed versions. Results cited from other studies, including the original single-direction study, are not treated as this study's results. Operating-point sweep values used only to select settings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study never computes, ablates or adds a residual-stream refusal direction or cone. It induces refusal on purpose by zeroing weight rows that a contrastive attribution score selects. Its main question is selector faithfulness: LRP and IG against baselines. The redundancy result is that LRP and IG top-1% row masks overlap only 3-6% yet both install refusal. That is weight-row redundancy: many disjoint row sets can push activations along the same downstream direction(s). So it cannot tell one residual direction from several, and does not bear on V4's affine, cone or dominant-plus-others geometry. The link to multi-direction work [35] is the authors' interpretation, not a measurement. The results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude attribution selectors are causally faithful at the language-modeling level and that contrastive attribution installs refusal specifically, beating layer-matched controls. Refusal lives in a redundant weight subspace (LRP and IG masks largely disjoint), so edits are sufficient realizations, not a unique mechanism, and necessity is not tested. Two additions: they call this redundancy consistent with, and predicted by, multi-direction activation-space accounts [35], without testing that link. They also stress that rank-stable selectors such as MeanActivation can be the least faithful, even reducing refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive harmful-versus-benign attribution to rank neuron rows and zeroes selected rows in instruction-tuned models. It does not calculate a residual-stream difference-in-means direction or project that direction out/add it across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by attribution method, architecture, harm domain, and selected operating point (lambda and sparsity k). The best method reverses across architectures; higher sparsity for lower-signal domains can damage capability.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing top-ranked rows by contrastive LRP or IG attribution (k≈0.5-15% of rows) raises CAST malign refusal, e.g. LLaMA-3.1-8B hate 0.488→0.82-0.85, with low benign over-refusal on hate and crime. Medical and legal need a larger k and lose capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be installed by ablating a sparse, attribution-selected set of weight rows (mostly MLP gate/up).

fits_no_version.finding: LRP and IG top-1% behavior masks overlap only 3-6% (Jaccard) across all four models and five domains. LRP vs a seeded-random mask overlaps about 0.5%. Both methods still install refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-row sets sufficient to install refusal are redundant: many largely disjoint row masks suffice.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-matched random masks reach a mean of 0.003-0.274 against 0.50-0.93 for the real LRP mask (LLaMA-3.1-8B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a selector's mask, row identity rather than depth allocation carries the refusal-installing effect.

record.problems: Refusal is scored with one classifier under greedy decoding; the authors note that both the contrastive target and classifier are sensitive to refusal-onset surface forms. Selector runs are single evaluations at fixed operating points; repeated-seed robustness is not generally reported. The layer-matched faithfulness control is reported only for LLaMA-3.1-8B-LRP. Stronger settings can increase over-refusal and damage utility, and medical/legal edits can collapse capability.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the five LLaMA-3.2-1B LRP-vs-IG top-1% Jaccard entries from Appendix E, Table 35 to remain within the 60-row limit while retaining every per-model/domain refusal outcome, the other three models' overlap entries, and the layer-matched controls. Table 35 reports the omitted overlaps as 0.051 (hate), 0.042 (crime), 0.042 (adult), 0.035 (medical), and 0.039 (legal). Other reported measures such as SorryBench, OR-Bench-Hard, benign over-refusal, and utility are not separate rows because they do not directly measure the V4 redundancy claim.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction; no directional ablation or activation addition; no capability check under such an intervention.
No refusal-removal weight edit or abliteration; removal masks were deliberately withheld.
No residual-stream affine, cone or multi-direction geometry measured; only weight-row mask overlap.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer of a direction across languages or variants.
No reasoning-model test; Qwen3-8B is treated as instruct and thinking is not analysed.

record.verdict_notes: Re-classified from tests/T5 to discusses/T6. The study is a selector-faithfulness audit that induces refusal by weight-row zeroing. It cites the single-direction paper and the cone paper but measures neither directional ablation nor residual geometry. Disjoint weight-row masks are compatible with a single residual direction, since different rows can write onto the same direction. So the V4 'supports' label is unwarranted. Several row notes cross-reference the wrong row ids.

versions.untested_parts: Does not find and ablate/add the harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction, test all-layer/all-position projection, or assess general capability under that intervention.
Installs refusal by zeroing contrastively selected neuron rows; does not test refusal-removal weight edits or released abliteration.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
Tests redundant neuron-row masks that install refusal, not residual-stream affine/cone geometry or whether there is a dominant direction plus smaller directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Recomputes contrastive row selectors per model; does not test whether the same direction transfers across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing.

relation.reason: Cites Arditi et al. [29] and Wollschläger et al. [35] in related work, and in Sec 5.5 argues weight-space redundancy mirrors multi-direction refusal, without testing it.

tranche.reason: No residual-stream direction or cone is computed, ablated or added. Direction-based selectors are stated out of scope. Weight-row redundancy is related to [35] only by argument, not tested in activation space.

source_check.notes: The record says T6 with no verdicts, yet 15 of its 16 checked rows are still linked to V4 (as observed or absent); only r01 was relinked to none, so the links should be cleared. Layer-matched controls on LLaMA-3.1-8B hate fall below the unedited baseline (0.488 -> mean 0.274). Row baselines in r56-r60 are the real LRP mask, not the unedited model.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LRP and IG contrastive masks across the tested instruction-tuned models and CAST domains
reader_labels.reason: The methods install refusal despite low top-1% mask overlap (3-6% reported; rows r41-r55), while the layer-matched random controls do not reproduce LRP's effect (r56-r60). The study supports redundant sufficient row masks, not a specific residual-stream geometry.
